solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One overseeing area where Jesus once rested

indicators.note: area where Jesus rested reads as the area sitting in the place he rested, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: the infant Jesus was laid in a manger, the feeding trough of the nativity

explanation.surface: A supervisor is pictured looking after the stable from the nativity story.
explanation.walkthrough: The nativity manger has A for area placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss or supervisor is someone who oversees staff or a business.

clue.text: Nameless guards cool in centre of vessel

indicators.note: nameless means without a name, so N for name is removed

parts.note: to mind is to guard or look after
hip means cool or fashionable

explanation.surface: Anonymous security men stay calm in the middle of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: Located midway along a ship's length is in the centre of a vessel.

clue.text: Lure man after shaking figure

indicators.note: after shaking means once these letters are jumbled about

explanation.surface: A man is enticed once he has been shaken up.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is a written symbol for a number, like 7 or VII.

clue.text: Literally, beginning to go south — European birds

parts.note: the beginning of go is the letter G, and literally means spelt out as a word, which is gee

explanation.surface: European birds begin heading south for the winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literally' asks for the letter G written out in full rather than as a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of goose: waterfowl, which are birds.

clue.text: Forever a scallywag? Just a bit

definitions.text: Forever a scallywag? Just a bit

indicators.note: just a bit means only part of these words is taken, the answer lying inside them

explanation.surface: Is someone a permanent rogue, or only slightly so?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a scallywag is a mild rogue, which is just a bit of a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a mischievous rogue or scamp, a near synonym.

clue.text: Solidified material after fire's curtailed

parts.note: a cryptic description of volcanic rock: frothy lava that sets hard once the eruption's fire dies down

explanation.surface: Something hardens once a blaze has been put out.
explanation.walkthrough: The fire is a volcano's: when the eruption ends, the frothy lava cools into a light, porous stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Light porous volcanic rock forms when gassy lava cools and sets solid after an eruption.

clue.text: Sort of superior, leader of site for nun, essentially

definitions.meaning: a kind of religious superior, a nun ranking just below an abbess

definitions.text: leader of site for nun, essentially
definitions.meaning: the head of a priory, the house where a community of nuns lives

explanation.walkthrough: Mother Superior is the title of the nun in charge; this is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The nun heading a priory is a superior, in charge of the nuns living there.

clue.text: After casing area, Scottish engineer set up excellent plant

indicators.note: casing means enclosing, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: John McAdam was the Scottish engineer behind macadamised roads

indicators.note: in a down answer set up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A Scottish engineer surrounds a site and then sets up a fine plant.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first class, is treated as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian nut tree is a plant, grown for its edible nuts.

clue.text: With another, this man on board gets a country house

definitions.text: With another, this man on board gets a country house

parts.words: With another, this man on board gets a country house
parts.note: a piece on a draughts board; add another and the plural names the Prime Minister's country residence

explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country house in Buckinghamshire; draughts is the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughts piece is a man on the board, and two or more give the PM's country retreat.

clue.text: Stupid me — this screw mangled adjustable controls

parts.note: dim means stupid

indicators.note: something mangled is crushed out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone berates themselves for ruining a screw while doing some DIY.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid me' reads as one exclamation, but 'Stupid' alone gives its synonym and 'me' joins the fodder; 'mangled' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Light fittings that let you vary brightness are adjustable controls on lamps.

clue.text: Heavens! You don't want English sports equipment

indicators.note: not wanting something means leaving it out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: the skies are the heavens

explanation.surface: An exclamation that you'd better not buy English sporting kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens!' looks like an exclamation, but it is the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Long runners for gliding over snow are kit used in a winter sport.

clue.text: Reportedly, harsh jumper's made from animal product

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are heard rather than read, a sound-alike

parts.note: harsh means hoarse, and a jumper is a hare

explanation.surface: A rough knitted sweater is said to be made from something taken from an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a woolly sweater, but here it is the leaping hare; HOARSE HARE said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair from a horse's mane or tail is a product taken from an animal, used in brushes and upholstery.

clue.text: High, continued demand for product in Denmark

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: DK is the international abbreviation for Denmark
a run on something is sustained heavy demand for it

explanation.surface: Demand for some Danish product remains strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like it describes the demand, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: High as in intoxicated: both words describe being under the influence of alcohol.

clue.text: Poirot heartlessly arrests that girl in French ball

indicators.note: a detective who arrests someone holds them, so one piece is held inside the other
heartlessly removes everything but the outer letters of the word

parts.note: elle is French for she

explanation.surface: Hercule Poirot detains a young woman at a French dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' looks like a dance to go with the French girl, but it is a small round object.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny compressed sphere, such as shot or feed, is a small ball.

clue.text: Welsh girl's supporting sibling's son shunning outsiders for book

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means placed underneath
shunning outsiders drops the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: your brother's or sister's son is your nephew
Sian is a Welsh girl's name, with the s from the possessive

explanation.surface: A Welsh girl backs her nephew who avoids strangers for a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's letter to the church at Ephesus is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Frank's initially ignored outdated foreign bread

indicators.note: the opening letter is ignored, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to frank a letter is to stamp it, so franks are postmarks

explanation.surface: Frank snubbed someone at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the verb meaning to stamp mail; 'bread' is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of former East Germany is obsolete foreign money, and bread is slang for cash.

clue.text: Split before end of drama on Channel 4

definitions.note: the cross-reference to the answer of 4 down, a scallywag

parts.note: to split is to tear

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of the word

parts.note: a way is a channel or route

explanation.surface: A split happens before the end of a drama on the TV station Channel 4.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel 4' looks like the British TV station, but '4' is the definition, pointing to 4 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild, reckless youngster is much the same as a rascal or scallywag.

clue.text: Opponents go after two Greek characters eating new snack food

indicators.note: go after places this piece at the end
eating takes something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: mu and chi are letters of the Greek alphabet
East and South are opposing partnerships at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Rivals pursue a couple of Greek people who are eating a new snack.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, East and South sit on opposing sides, so ES are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, snacks and nibbles are called this, from the urge to eat something.

clue.text: Second group of sailors giving time of day to poet

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A second crew of sailors gives a poet the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for morning, the start of the day, used in verse.

clue.text: One Python character brought up swallows originally of African place

indicators.note: swallows takes something inside
in a down answer brought up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Brian is the hero of the Monty Python film Life of Brian

indicators.note: originally means the first letter

parts.note: I is one

explanation.surface: A Monty Python character is raised and gulps down something from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns IBORIAN (I plus BRIAN around O) round.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Kenya is a place in Africa.

clue.text: Three females embracing a journalist messed about

indicators.note: embracing holds something inside, so the letter goes within the others

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, so three of them give FFF
ED is short for editor, the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A trio of women hug a reporter, who then wasted time.
explanation.definitionFit: Faffing about is British slang for dithering or fussing, the same as messing about.

clue.text: Fellow with issue makes us quiver

parts.note: issue means offspring, as does a litter

explanation.surface: A man with a problem makes us tremble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a problem, but it means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: To flutter or tremble rapidly is to quiver.

clue.text: Documentary evidence about leopard regularly finding shade

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a deed is a legal document that serves as evidence

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter

explanation.surface: A documentary about a leopard often finds it in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Documentary' suggests a film, but a deed is a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark crimson is a shade, meaning a colour.

clue.text: Axes, bats or bombs?

indicators.note: bombs as a verb means fails badly or crashes, so these letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A list of weapons: axes, bats, or bombs?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like plural choppers, but it is a verb meaning cancels.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe a project and to call it off both mean cancelling it.

clue.text: European city on island — address for woman

parts.note: re means on, as in regarding
Ms is a title used to address a woman

explanation.surface: A place on an island is given as a woman's address.
explanation.definitionFit: The French cathedral city in Champagne is a European city.

clue.text: Mechanical tool biker fabricated

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so these letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: A biker has made some mechanical tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting like a machine is mechanical, in an automaton's unthinking way.

clue.text: Article on Middle East topic

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on Middle East matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject under discussion is a topic.

clue.text: New career low, Tory conceals capital in Swiss pottery brand

indicators.note: conceals hides one piece inside the other
new means made afresh, so these letters are rearranged
the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Conservative at the low point of a career hides money in a Swiss account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money or Bern, but it is the first letter of Swiss, which goes inside the rearranged CAREER LOW TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: This English porcelain maker is a well-known name in fine china and pottery.

clue.text: Without glasses — not content, feel for pen

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to feel for someone is to pity them

indicators.note: not content empties a word of its inside, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone without spectacles is unhappy and reaches for a pen by touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feel for' looks like groping, and 'pen' looks like a writing tool, but it is an enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is an enclosure for animals, and a sty is one for pigs.

clue.text: Quietly covered up by marine, wine is spiked

indicators.note: covered up by means held inside the following piece

parts.note: marine means relating to the sea
P is piano, quietly in music
red is a wine

explanation.surface: A marine secretly hides the fact that his wine has been laced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiked' suggests a drugged drink, but it means pierced with a spear.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierced with a spear is spiked, run through with a pointed object.
